map.summary: The foundation subsystem is the shared base layer of a multi-tenant hybrid RAG service: a create_app FastAPI entry point exposing health/readiness and an evaluation router, a cached typed Settings boundary, an async SQLAlchemy Base, a tenant-scoped DocumentService over replaceable file storage, and a linear Alembic chain defining identity, content, retrieval, evaluation/audit, and ingestion-job schema. Migrations push authorization, lifecycle, lease, and immutability invariants into PostgreSQL, while a Dockerfile, Makefile, Compose, and CI provide orchestration and verification.
unknowns: No user-facing retrieval or answers HTTP routes appear in this batch beyond health and the mounted evaluation router, so the wider application surface is untraced (F0002).
Runtime code that populates documents.storage_key/index_version, ingestion_jobs.checkpoint and pipeline_version, and query_traces fields is absent (F0032, F0064).

Whether LocalFileStorage is the implementation actually injected into the runtime DocumentService, and whether the ORM models or migrations are the operative schema, is not directly evidenced (F0080).

How Dramatiq workers are started and how Redis is bound to ingestion job execution is not shown; only a heartbeat actor, the declared dependency, and a local Redis container are evidenced (F0016, F0096).
Callers that generate AuditEvent.action namespaced strings, and consumers of the content-hash index, are not present in these sources (F0032, F0079).
Whether FastAPI health and evaluation endpoints are consumed by the frontend or external actors is not evidenced.

diagrams.title: Architecture
diagrams.description: The FastAPI app reads shared Settings and mounts health and evaluation routes; the same Settings feeds schema management and dependency probes. Makefile, Compose, and CI form the orchestration boundary around app, schema, and tests.

diagrams.title: Tenancy and persistence
diagrams.description: Tenant ownership is structural: composite tenant-scoped foreign keys and uniqueness let PostgreSQL reject cross-tenant references, while immutability triggers and status checks push lifecycle invariants out of application code.

diagrams.title: Health and dependency probing
diagrams.description: Liveness is a static response; readiness fans out concurrent probes against configured external dependencies and returns 503 when any probe reports false, isolating partial failure.

diagrams.title: Document lifecycle service
diagrams.description: DocumentService owns transactions and requires an already authorized tenant/collection scope. Upload locks the collection to serialize dedupe and stages the file off the event loop; delete commits intent before removing storage, accepting non-atomic DB and disk.

diagrams.title: External integration and async boundary
diagrams.description: Settings names every external dependency the backend expects, including Cohere providers and Redis/Dramatiq; however these sources show configuration and a worker actor but no runtime wiring that connects them to ingestion execution.

F0001.statement: The backend ships as a single uvicorn-served FastAPI application created by create_app and exposed as hybrid_rag_search.main:app, with PYTHONPATH and --app-dir pointing at /app/src so the installed package is importable (S0001, S0004).

F0002.statement: create_app wires two route groups: liveness responses shared by /health and /health/live, a /health/ready readiness handler that returns 503 when dependency_status(settings) reports any false dependency, and the evaluation router mounted via include_router (S0004).

F0003.statement: The application reads configuration once per create_app call through get_settings(); liveness and readiness both depend on that settings object for environment and dependency probing (S0004).

F0004.statement: Alembic migration environment derives its async SQLAlchemy URL from the same get_settings().database_url used by the application, converting it via async_database_url and setting target_metadata to the shared Base.metadata (S0010).

F0005.statement: migrations/env.py supports both offline literal-bind generation and online execution through async_engine_from_config with NullPool, running migrations inside run_sync(do_run_migrations) (S0010).

F0006.statement: The migration workflow is documented as a Make/Alembic-driven lifecycle: db-revision autogenerates, db-upgrade applies head, db-downgrade reverts one revision, and db-seed loads deterministic dev records (S0002, S0009).

F0007.statement: The Makefile is the local orchestration boundary: it provisions the venv and dependencies (setup), runs backend and frontend dev servers together with uvicorn over the backend/src layout, and exposes Docker Compose stack targets for the local environment (S0009).

F0008.statement: The infra boundary owns local infrastructure configuration under the root compose.yaml, pinning ARM64 images for Python, Node, PostgreSQL, Redis, and OpenSearch, restricting published ports to 127.0.0.1 and disabling OpenSearch security for local use only (S0005).

F0009.statement: The Makefile exposes operational entry points for non-HTTP subsystems as python -m modules: tokenizer_setup, ingestion_recovery, index_rebuild (start/promote), and evaluation.scifact (download/validate/subset) alongside evaluation.runner prepare/run (S0009).

F0010.statement: CI runs the backend as a separate job against service containers for OpenSearch 3.6.0 (single-node, security disabled) and PostgreSQL 17.11, with DATABASE_URL pointing at the service Postgres, then lints, type-checks, runs pytest, exercises Alembic upgrade/check/downgrade/upgrade, seeds twice, and runs integration-marked tests (S0006).

F0011.statement: CI runs a parallel frontend job over frontend/ with npm ci, format check, lint, typecheck, test, and build, indicating the frontend is built and validated independently of the Python backend (S0006).

F0012.statement: The pyproject declares runtime integrations used by the backend (asyncpg, SQLAlchemy asyncio, Alembic, Redis, Dramatiq[redis], Cohere, httpx, pypdf, markdown-it-py, tokenizers) and defines pytest markers 'integration' (migrated local PostgreSQL) and 'live' (authorized external provider calls) that gate environments with external dependencies (S0003).

F0013.statement: The backend package is restrictively typed and tested: hatchling builds src/hybrid_rag_search, mypy runs strict over the package, and pytest enforces 100% coverage excluding integration and live tests (S0003).

F0014.statement: Local development hooks couple Python and frontend tooling via pre-commit: ruff check/format on Python files and prettier check over frontend/ assets share a single commit-time gate (S0008).

F0015.statement: A separate repository-map workflow publishes documentation assets (maps, overview, manifest) to a dedicated 'repo-map' branch and to run artifacts, gated to the default branch and serialized through a concurrency group; it is documentation tooling, not application runtime (S0007).

F0016.statement: The Dockerfile installs the package from pyproject.toml and src and then launches uvicorn as the container CMD; there is no evidence in these sources of a Dramatiq worker process being launched by the same image (S0001).

F0017.statement: Migration 20260915_01 creates the identity schema (tenants, users, memberships) and defines a set_updated_at() PL/pgSQL trigger function that sets updated_at on BEFORE UPDATE for each of the three tables.

F0018.statement: Tenants enforce a lowercase hyphenated slug format via ck_tenants_slug_format and a unique constraint uq_tenants_slug, while users enforce normalized lowercase email via ck_users_email_normalized and uq_users_email.

F0019.statement: Memberships bind user to tenant with role constrained to owner/admin/member, cascade-delete foreign keys to tenants and users, and composite uniqueness uq_memberships_tenant_id_user_id plus uq_memberships_tenant_id_id supporting tenant-scoped references.

F0020.statement: Migration 20260915_02 revises 20260915_01 and creates collections, collection_grants, documents, and ingestion_jobs, reusing set_updated_at() triggers across all four new tables.

F0021.statement: collection_grants references collections and memberships through tenant-scoped composite foreign keys (tenant_id, collection_id) and (tenant_id, membership_id), both cascade-delete, with permission constrained to read/write/manage.

F0022.statement: Documents carry a sha256 content_hash constraint, a status lifecycle (pending/processing/ready/failed/deleting/deleted) reconciled with deleted_at via ck_documents_deleted_at_matches_status, a monotonic index_version starting at 0, a non-blank storage_key and source_key, and JSONB source_metadata defaulting to '{}'.

F0023.statement: Documents reference collections with ondelete RESTRICT and enforce per-tenant per-collection source deduplication via uq_documents_tenant_id_collection_id_source_key; indexes ix_documents_content_hash and ix_documents_tenant_status support hash lookup and status filtering.

F0024.statement: ingestion_jobs belong to a document via tenant-scoped composite FK that cascades on delete, track status (queued/running/succeeded/failed/cancelled), attempts bounded by max_attempts via ck_ingestion_jobs_attempts_within_limit, a JSONB checkpoint defaulting to '{}', and started_at/finished_at timestamps.

F0025.statement: Migration 20260915_03 revises 20260915_02 and introduces a prevent_mutation() PL/pgSQL function that raises an integrity_constraint_violation exception for BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE, used to make retrieval_configs append-only.

F0026.statement: retrieval_configs store per-tenant versioned retrieval parameters as JSONB (validated as an object), an embedding_model required non-blank, an optional rerank_model, and uniqueness on (tenant_id, name, version); the immutability trigger blocks updates and deletes.

F0027.statement: query_traces record per-query diagnostics: normalized_query_hash (sha256 format), nullable query_text gated by content_captured via ck_query_traces_query_text_capture_policy, selected_path, total_latency_ms, and JSONB timings/rankings/usage/fallbacks plus nullable error.

F0028.statement: query_traces reference collections and retrieval_configs via tenant-scoped composite foreign keys with ondelete RESTRICT, so trace history preserves the collection and retrieval config it was produced against.

F0029.statement: The three migrations form a linear revision chain (20260915_01 -> 20260915_02 -> 20260915_03) with each downgrade dropping its tables and trigger functions in reverse order, and downgrade of 20260915_03 drops the immutable trigger before the retrieval_configs table.

F0030.statement: Schema-level invariants enforced in PostgreSQL rather than application code include email normalization, slug format, role and permission enumeration, status enumeration for documents and ingestion jobs, and the deleted_at/status consistency check.

F0031.statement: Multi-tenancy is enforced structurally: collection_grants, documents, ingestion_jobs, retrieval_configs, and query_traces all carry tenant_id and use tenant-scoped composite foreign keys or uniqueness so cross-tenant references are rejected at the database level.

F0032.statement: Content-hash indexing (ix_documents_content_hash) and the sha256 content_hash constraint suggest deduplication or hash-based lookup of document content, but no runtime consumer of these indexes appears in this migration batch.

F0033.statement: Migration 20260915_04 creates the evaluation_datasets, judgments, evaluation_runs, and audit_events tables, forming the evaluation and audit schema domain in the linear Alembic chain (down_revision 20260915_03).

F0034.statement: Tenant ownership is enforced structurally: judgments and evaluation_runs reference evaluation_datasets via composite (tenant_id, dataset_id) foreign keys, so a judgment or run can only attach to a dataset of the same tenant.

F0035.statement: Evaluation datasets, judgments, and audit_events are declared immutable: the migration attaches a BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger executing prevent_mutation() to each of those three tables, so rows are append-only once written.

F0036.statement: evaluation_runs carries an explicit lifecycle (status constrained to queued/running/succeeded/failed/cancelled by ck_evaluation_runs_status_allowed) with started_at/finished_at timestamps, while its updated_at is maintained by a set_updated_at() trigger rather than by application code.

F0037.statement: Deleting an evaluation_datasets row cascades to its judgments (ondelete CASCADE on fk_judgments_tenant_id_evaluation_datasets) but is restricted when referenced by evaluation_runs (ondelete RESTRICT), so dataset history required by runs is preserved.

F0038.statement: Migration 20260918_05 adds a durable 'stage' column to ingestion_jobs constrained to parse/chunk/embed/index/complete, and ck_ingestion_jobs_completion_matches_status ties (status = 'succeeded') to (stage = 'complete') so success and completion cannot diverge.

F0039.statement: Migration 20260918_06 makes ingestion identity content-addressed and pipeline-versioned: content_hash (backfilled from documents.content_hash) and pipeline_version become NOT NULL with format checks, and uq_ingestion_jobs_document_recipe makes (tenant_id, document_id, content_hash, pipeline_version) unique, defining job reuse per document recipe.

F0040.statement: Ingestion worker ownership is an expiring lease: migration 20260918_07 adds lease_token and lease_expires_at with ck_ingestion_jobs_lease_matches_running requiring (status = 'running') to equal both lease columns being NOT NULL, plus ix_ingestion_jobs_status_lease for scanning expired leases.

F0041.statement: Retry scheduling is durable in the database: next_attempt_at with ck_ingestion_jobs_retry_time_requires_queued (a retry time may only exist when status = 'queued') and index ix_ingestion_jobs_status_retry.

F0042.statement: These migration constraints push ingestion orchestration semantics (stage progression, deduplicated recipes, lease-based recovery, retry eligibility) into PostgreSQL rather than leaving them solely to application code, and consumers are expected to observe them.

F0043.statement: Settings (backend/src/hybrid_rag_search/config.py) is a cached (lru_cache on get_settings) Pydantic BaseSettings loaded from environment/.env, exposing database_url, redis_url, opensearch_url, storage/tokenizer/ingestion artifact roots, and Cohere embedding/rerank/generation parameters with timeouts and pricing.

F0044.statement: External integrations are configurable through Settings: PostgreSQL (database_url), Redis (redis_url), OpenSearch (opensearch_url plus read/write aliases and index schema version), and Cohere (COHERE_API_KEY or COHERE_TRIAL_KEY secret, models, timeouts, and USD pricing for embedding, rerank, and generation tokens).

F0045.statement: Settings.validate_cross_field_settings enforces startup invariants across configuration: embed-english-light-v3.0 requires cohere_embed_dimensions == 384, rerank_result_limit may not exceed rerank_candidate_limit, and cohere_rerank_timeout_seconds may not exceed retrieval_deadline_seconds.

F0046.statement: Retrieval tuning limits (opensearch_bm25_candidate_limit, opensearch_dense_candidate_limit, rerank_candidate_limit, rerank_result_limit) and retrieval_deadline_seconds are declared as positive bounded settings, providing a shared configuration boundary for the retrieval and rerank stages.

F0047.statement: The settings module is the only configuration boundary in this batch that pairs the embedding model with the OpenSearch index schema version (opensearch_index_schema_version = 'chunks-v3'), which its validator docstring ties to the chunks index mapping dimensions.

F0048.statement: The package initiation file identifies hybrid_rag_search as the API package, while the settings module (config.py) holds runtime cross-dependency configuration rather than retrieval or ingestion logic, consistent with a foundation layer shared by the answers, ingestion, and retrieval subsystems.

F0049.statement: database.py defines a shared SQLAlchemy DeclarativeBase named Base whose MetaData uses a NAMING_CONVENTION for indexes, unique, check, foreign key, and primary key constraints; the docstring states it is shared by application models and Alembic.

F0050.statement: async_database_url() rewrites a 'postgresql' drivername URL to 'postgresql+asyncpg' and returns other drivers unchanged, so the project's async PostgreSQL driver is applied centrally.

F0051.statement: models/__init__.py re-exports domain model classes across content, evaluation, identity, and retrieval modules, making models a single public import surface for collections, documents, ingestion jobs, evaluation artifacts, tenancy, and retrieval config/traces.

F0052.statement: content.py models enforce multi-tenant ownership via composite, tenant-scoped foreign keys: CollectionGrant references [tenant_id, collection_id] and [tenant_id, membership_id], Document references [tenant_id, collection_id], and IngestionJob references [tenant_id, document_id].

F0053.statement: Document lifecycle state is a constrained text column whose allowed values are pending, processing, ready, failed, deleting, deleted, with a CHECK enforcing that deleted_at is non-null exactly when status is 'deleted'.

F0054.statement: Document identity is deduplicated per collection: UniqueConstraint('tenant_id', 'collection_id', 'source_key') plus a SHA-256 format CHECK on content_hash, and DocumentService sets source_key to the document UUID string.

F0055.statement: IngestionJob schema carries queued/running/succeeded/failed/cancelled status, parse/chunk/embed/index/complete stages, attempts and max_attempts, checkpoint JSONB, and lease fields, with CHECK constraints tying running status to a live lease and succeeded status to the complete stage; the unique key is (tenant_id, document_id, content_hash, pipeline_version).

F0056.statement: DocumentService owns its transactions and requires callers to supply an already authorized tenant/collection scope, delegating duplicate detection, upload, fetch, and delete without performing authorization itself.

F0057.statement: DocumentService.upload hashes content, takes a row lock on the collection via with_for_update() to serialize duplicate checks across concurrent uploads, returns an existing non-deleting document as a duplicate, and otherwise inserts a PENDING Document then saves the file via asyncio.to_thread outside the event loop.

F0058.statement: DocumentService.delete commits DELETING intent in one transaction, then in a second transaction removes the file and marks the document DELETED with deleted_at set; the docstring documents that PostgreSQL and disk cannot commit atomically, so a crash may orphan a file but must not delete a possibly committed original.

F0059.statement: DocumentService._document guards against corrupted or cross-tenant storage pointers by verifying document.storage_key equals storage_key(tenant_id, document_id) and raises ValueError on mismatch, in addition to tenant-scoped lookup.

F0060.statement: health.py provides check_postgres (asyncpg SELECT 1), check_redis (Redis PING), and check_opensearch (HTTP GET /_cluster/health with raise_for_status), and dependency_status fans these out concurrently via asyncio.gather, returning booleans keyed by 'postgres', 'redis', 'opensearch'.

F0061.statement: run_check isolates probe failure by catching Exception and returning False, so an unreachable dependency yields a false status rather than propagating an error to callers.

F0062.statement: health probes read connection targets from Settings (database_url, redis_url, opensearch_url), making Settings the single configuration surface for external dependency checks.

F0063.statement: DocumentService receives an async_sessionmaker[AsyncSession] and a FileStorage collaborator plus a storage_key helper from hybrid_rag_search.storage, establishing storage as a separate subsystem that DocumentService calls off the event loop.

F0064.statement: The module docstring of documents.py describes the file as original-file lifecycle independent of HTTP and future ingestion workers, indicating the service is intended as a domain layer decoupled from transport and worker orchestration.

F0065.statement: The evaluation, identity, and retrieval ORM modules all declare SQLAlchemy models against the shared hybrid_rag_search.database.Base registry, making Base the single metadata aggregation point for these persistence domains.

F0066.statement: All three model modules use PostgreSQL-specific column types (JSONB and UUID via sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql) rather than portable types, binding the schema to PostgreSQL.

F0067.statement: Cross-module ownership is enforced through tenant-scoped composite foreign keys: Judgment and EvaluationRun reference evaluation_datasets via (tenant_id, dataset_id), QueryTrace references collections and retrieval_configs via (tenant_id, x_id), and AuditEvent references memberships via (tenant_id, actor_membership_id).

F0068.statement: Domain invariants are pushed into the database as CheckConstraints in the model layer: corpus_hash and normalized_query_hash must match '^[0-9a-f]{64}$' (SHA-256), relevance_grade must be in 0..3, evaluation run status must be one of the EvaluationRunStatus values, and AuditEvent.action must match a namespaced 'domain.verb' pattern.

F0069.statement: Identity models define Tenant, User, and Membership with a tenant_id+user_id uniqueness constraint on memberships and a role CheckConstraint restricting roles to 'owner','admin','member' matching the MembershipRole StrEnum.

F0070.statement: EvaluationDataset, RetrievalConfig, and AuditEvent carry tenant_id foreign keys with differing delete behavior on tenants.id: CASCADE for datasets/collections/configs versus RESTRICT for audit events, indicating audit history is intentionally retained even if a tenant is removed.

F0071.statement: EvaluationRun references its dataset and retrieval config with ondelete='RESTRICT', meaning a dataset or retrieval config that has been evaluated cannot be deleted while a run exists.

F0072.statement: EvaluationRun tracks asynchronous lifecycle via status (defaulting to EvaluationRunStatus.QUEUED), started_at, finished_at, error_message, and a JSONB metrics column, with updated_at maintained by SQLAlchemy onupdate.

F0073.statement: QueryTrace models a per-query observability record with selected_path, timings, rankings, usage, fallbacks, and error fields, and enforces a capture policy: 'content_captured OR query_text IS NULL' so raw query text is only stored when content capture is enabled.

F0074.statement: seed.py is a standalone orchestration entry point separate from the FastAPI app: it builds an async engine from Settings.database_url and executes idempotent upsert statements (insert(...).on_conflict_do_update) for Tenant, User, Membership, Collection, and CollectionGrant under fixed demo UUIDs.

F0075.statement: seed.py imports Collection and CollectionGrant from hybrid_rag_search.models, which these sources do not define, showing the models package re-exports content-domain models owned elsewhere.

F0076.statement: storage.py defines a FileStorage Protocol (save/fetch/delete) as a replaceable storage boundary; storage_key(tenant_id, document_id) returns '{tenant_id}/{document_id}' and explicitly excludes upload filenames from keys.

F0077.statement: LocalFileStorage implements the protocol with create-only atomic writes: it validates keys against a canonical-UUID pattern, rejects symlinked path components, writes to a sibling tempfile that is fsync'd, then publishes via os.link so an existing original is never overwritten.

F0078.statement: AuditEvent is modeled as an append-only-style record (entity_type/entity_id/action/details JSONB plus occurred_at) whose actor is optional via a nullable actor_membership_id, allowing events without an authenticated membership actor.

F0079.statement: The AuditEvent.action namespaced-format CheckConstraint implies runtime callers generate actions as '<domain>.<verb>' strings; no such callers are present in these sources.

F0080.statement: Because the sources only show model declarations and the seed script, whether LocalFileStorage is the storage implementation actually injected into the runtime DocumentService, and whether these models are the operative schema versus migration-managed DDL, is not directly evidenced here.

F0081.statement: DocumentService is constructed with an async session factory and a storage backend, and tests instantiate it directly over async_sessionmaker plus LocalFileStorage, placing transaction ownership inside the service rather than in a router.

F0082.statement: DocumentService.upload-hashes content (sha256, e.g. the hash of b"hello" is asserted), records original_filename, size_bytes, media_type and content_hash, and persists the document with DocumentStatus.PENDING.

F0083.statement: DocumentService.upload performs a deduplication lookup via session.scalar keyed on content hash and returns the existing document with duplicate=true instead of inserting again; a second upload of identical bytes adds no new row.

F0084.statement: storage_key(tenant_id, document_id) is the derived object key, and fetch validates that the stored pointer's tenant identity matches the caller; a mismatched key raises ValueError before deletion.

F0085.statement: Tenant isolation is enforced across fetch/delete/upload: operations attempted by another tenant on an existing document raise DocumentNotFound rather than exposing its existence.

F0086.statement: Document deletion is two-phase: the document is first marked DocumentStatus.DELETING, then the storage delete runs; if storage.delete raises OSError the status remains DELETING and fetch raises DocumentUnavailable, and a retry completes with DocumentStatus.DELETED plus deleted_at set.

F0087.statement: Deleting an already-deleted document is idempotent (repeated delete succeeds), and after successful deletion the blob is absent while a subsequent identical upload creates a new document_id (not flagged duplicate).

F0088.statement: If storage.save fails during upload (OSError), the exception propagates and no Document row for that filename is persisted, indicating the file write is staged before/around the DB write.

F0089.statement: IngestionJob schema constrains its state machine in PostgreSQL: stage defaults to "parse" with ck_ingestion_jobs_stage_allowed, plus ck_ingestion_jobs_completion_matches_status, ck_ingestion_jobs_content_hash_sha256, ck_ingestion_jobs_pipeline_version_format, uq_ingestion_jobs_document_recipe, ck_ingestion_jobs_lease_matches_running, and ck_ingestion_jobs_retry_time_requires_queued.

F0090.statement: IngestionJob has status/lease and status/retry indexes (ix_ingestion_jobs_status_lease, ix_ingestion_jobs_status_retry), consistent with workers claiming leased jobs and retryable jobs.

F0091.statement: Base.metadata carries a shared NAMING_CONVENTION (pk_%(table_name)s and fk_%(table_name)s-prefixed names) asserted identical between database and test modules, making constraint names stable across the Base and migrations.

F0092.statement: async_database_url rewrites a plain postgresql URL to the postgresql+asyncpg driver and leaves an already-async URL unchanged, matching the health check which connects with asyncpg.connect.

F0093.statement: The health module exposes per-dependency probes (check_postgres executing SELECT 1 and closing its asyncpg connection, check_redis pinging and rejecting a false ping, check_opensearch requesting <host>/_cluster/health) plus run_check, which converts a probe exception into False and success into True.

F0094.statement: dependency_status fans the three named probes into a {postgres, redis, opensearch: bool} mapping, and the readiness endpoint returns 200 with status ready when all are true and 503 with not_ready when any probe is false.

F0095.statement: create_app() builds the FastAPI application used by tests via TestClient, serving /health, /health/live (both {"status":"ok","environment":"development"}) and /health/ready.

F0096.statement: The worker module exposes a Dramatiq actor heartbeat whose .fn() returns "ok", imported by the health/dependency test module alongside Settings and health probes.
